name: Vex & Ruin Synthskin Rave Shell
description:
A sleeveless shell jacket in sound-reactive photochromic fabric — matte black at rest, erupting into cascading violet-to-amber pulse patterns triggered by bass frequencies above 60Hz. The outer layer is laser-cut into overlapping scale segments that vibrate independently in high-pressure sound environments, creating a shimmer effect visible across a crowded floor. Interior lining is bioluminescent mesh in cyan, glowing passively between beats.

Vex & Ruin is a Circuit-born street label with no corponation licensing. The cut accommodates spinal rigs and neural port clusters at the collar. Wrist cuffs carry embedded haptic strips that sync to shared DJ broadcast signals.
functionality: Sound-reactive chromatic display. Haptic cuffs sync to venue broadcast frequency for crowd-shared tactile experience. Spinal rig channel built into back seam. Sealed against sweat and fog-machine particulate.
what_it_says: This person lives for the floor and knows exactly which underground parties to find.
manufacturer: Vex & Ruin (unlicensed street label, Circuit district)
story_hooks: The haptic sync frequency in a batch of Vex & Ruin shells has been hijacked — wearers at a rave receive a subliminal data-burst embedded in the tactile signal.
A Tier 4 corporate events planner is trying to track down who runs Vex & Ruin to license the tech — the label's founders are refusing and going deeper underground.
A runner uses the photochromic burst pattern as a dead-drop signal in a crowded club, visible only to someone who knows what sequence to watch for.
